messages.content: "你能幫我找到一家泰式餐廳在紐約的10英里範圍內嗎？然後再找一家義式餐廳在同一地點，同樣的距離內嗎？之後，你能提供過去一年亞馬遜雨林的降雨統計數據，然後是過去五年的嗎？"

function.name: ecology_data_precipitation_stats
function.description: Retrieve precipitation data for a specified location and time period. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The name of the location, e.g., 'Amazon rainforest'.

time_frame.description: The time period for which data is required.

function.name: restaurant_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby restaurants based on specific criteria like cuisine type. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Seattle, WA

cuisine.description: Preferred type of cuisine in restaurant.

max_distance.description: Maximum distance (in miles) within which to search for restaurants. Default is 5. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
The user wants:

1. Find Thai restaurant near New York within 10 miles.

2. Then find Italian restaurant at same place? They say "same location", maybe they mean also in NYC within 10 miles. So we need two separate queries: one Thai, one Italian.

We have tool `restaurant_find_nearby` with parameters: location string, cuisine string, max_distance optional default 5 but can set up to 10.

So call twice: first with location="New York City, NY" or just "NYC". Provide cuisine="Thai", max_distance=10. Second with cuisine="Italian".

Then retrieve precipitation stats for Amazon Rainforest over past year ("one year") and five years. Use `ecology_data_precipitation_stats`: location="Amazon rainforest", time_frame options: "six_months","year","five_years". We want both year and five_years. So call twice.

Thus produce calls accordingly.

We'll output JSON calls as per format. We'll do four calls sequentially.
